three_spin_binary.description: 15-site binary three-spin infinite-range energy prediction; paper reports EFNN relative error below 5e-3 for 2/3 layers with at least 105 neurons.

relative_error.description: Normalized binary energy RMSE; the paper's headline accuracy metric for the binary task.

rmse.description: Root mean squared energy error on the scored slice.

mae.description: Mean absolute energy error on the scored slice; rewards broadly accurate regression rather than optimizing only squared error.

tail_rmse.description: RMSE on the highest-energy-magnitude quartile; catches methods that fit only easy near-center configurations.

bias_abs.description: Absolute mean signed prediction error; penalizes systematic energy offsets that can hide behind aggregate RMSE.

pearson_corr.description: Linear correlation between predicted and true energies; catches constant-scale or collapsed-output shortcuts.

sign_accuracy.description: Fraction of nonzero-energy rows whose predicted energy has the correct sign.

neuron_count.description: Width of the submitted predictor; preserves the paper's compact-network constraint.

three_spin_continuous.description: 15-site continuous-spin three-body energy prediction; paper reports best 3-layer 150-neuron EFNN RMSE around 4e-2.

rmse.description: Root mean squared energy error; the paper's headline accuracy metric for the continuous task.

mae.description: Mean absolute energy error on the scored slice; rewards robust pointwise accuracy.

tail_rmse.description: RMSE on the highest-energy-magnitude quartile; checks whether continuous-spin accuracy holds on harder configurations.

bias_abs.description: Absolute mean signed prediction error; penalizes systematic energy offsets in continuous-spin predictions.

pearson_corr.description: Linear correlation between predicted and true energies; catches methods that match scale poorly or collapse predictions.

sign_accuracy.description: Fraction of nonzero-energy rows whose predicted energy has the correct sign.

neuron_count.description: Width of the submitted predictor; preserves the paper's compact-network constraint.
